description: We are a passionate and creative team interested in space, science, technology, and innovation. We bring together different skills and ideas to solve real-world challenges through teamwork, research, data analysis, and creative problem-solving. Our goal is to develop innovative solutions that can make a positive impact on Earth and beyond.
summary:
Astro Guardian is an interactive health-monitoring dashboard for astronauts on long space missions. Radiation, isolation, low gravity, and harsh conditions can affect the immune system, bone density, heart function, and mental health, while medical teams on Earth cannot always monitor astronauts in real time because of distance and communication delay.

We developed a web dashboard that brings health tracking and radiation monitoring into one system. It displays vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen, temperature), radiation dose rate, cumulative dose, and estimated safe exposure time, plus immune, bone-loss, and stress indicators. It classifies risk as Low, Medium, or High, shows alerts with suggested actions, supports crew monitoring, and exports mission data to CSV.

The current prototype uses simulated data, including a simulated solar storm. Our proposed full design uses Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and a scikit-learn Random Forest model.

Astro Guardian helps astronauts understand their condition, helps Mission Control detect risks earlier, and gives medical teams organized data for safer missions.
details:
؛ WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Astro Guardian is an interactive health-monitoring dashboard for astronauts on long space missions. It combines health tracking and radiation monitoring in one view. It shows vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, temperature), radiation dose rate, cumulative dose, and estimated safe exposure time, along with immune, bone-loss, and stress indicators and a daily mood check-in. A risk score classifies the astronaut's condition as Low, Medium, or High, and the dashboard shows alerts with suggested actions. It also supports crew monitoring and CSV export of mission data. A simulated solar storm and a storm shelter let users see how risk changes in real time.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Astronauts can understand their own condition and act on it early. Mission Control can detect risks sooner, and medical teams receive organized data for review. This matters most when communication with Earth is delayed.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

The dashboard is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, using Canvas and CSS 3D for visualization. We also prepared a Streamlit version and a proposed full architecture using Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and a scikit-learn Random Forest model for risk classification. The web dashboard itself uses rule-based risk scoring.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

The interface includes a live 3D radiation field showing solar particles around the spacecraft, and a rotating 3D cube whose faces show the status of the heart, lungs, immune system, bones, mind, and radiation. Information is organized so an astronaut can read their condition at a glance.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Radiation limits (NASA's 600 mSv career dose limit), long-term effects of low gravity on bones and the heart, immune and psychological health during isolation, communication delay with Earth, and clarity of information under stress.

CURRENT LIMITATIONS

This is a prototype that uses simulated data. Future work includes wearable sensors, training the model on real space and medical data, and improved communication with ground medical teams.
